messages:
Jules: hi all, first week here! trying to get a reproducible dev setup on WSL2 + VSCode Remote. hitting a few small headaches: asdf vs nodenv conflicts, gpg signing not working from VSCode, and op cli sessions not being seen by docker-compose. any checklist or tips?
Ravi: welcome Jules :wave: quick questions: are you opening your repo in the WSL window or from Windows path? that matters for which PATH is picked up.
Jules: opening in WSL. I installed asdf and brew inside WSL per the internal guide, but sometimes terminal says node v12 from /usr/bin rather than the asdf shim.
Priya: make sure your shell init loads asdf early. in ~/.profile or ~/.zshrc put the asdf export before any other PATH modifications. example:
```bash
export ASDF_DIR="$HOME/.asdf"
export PATH="$ASDF_DIR/bin:$ASDF_DIR/shims:$PATH"
. "$ASDF_DIR/asdf.sh"
```
Ravi: also check VSCode -> "Remote - WSL" is opening the folder. VSCode sometimes inherits Windows env if you start it from the Windows side. use the WSL command palette entry to open the folder.
Jules: that fixed the node shim problem. thanks. next: GPG signing. commits in the terminal show signed, but the VSCode source control UI shows unsigned and the commit pop-up asks for passphrase in a tiny window that disappears.
Priya: we run gpg inside WSL. install gnupg in the distro, import your key, and point git to it: `git config --global gpg.program /usr/bin/gpg`. also install pinentry-curses or pinentry-tty and configure `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf` with `pinentry-program /usr/bin/pinentry-curses` then `gpgconf --reload gpg-agent`.
Ravi: if you generated the key on another machine, export/transfer the private key via `gpg --export-secret-keys --armor KEYID | gpg --import` inside WSL.
DevOpsBot: Reminder: for GUI passphrase prompts under WSLg you can use `pinentry-gtk-2` if you want graphical prompt; install plus set pinentry-program accordingly.
Jules: great. last sticky bit: 1Password CLI (op). I run `eval $(op signin my)` in my shell and the token is there, but docker-compose env interpolation that uses ${REDWOOD_API_KEY} doesn't see it when run from VSCode tasks.
Priya: VSCode tasks spawn a non-interactive shell that may not source your interactive rc files. put the op signin eval in ~/.profile or create a small `~/.profile.d/op.sh` that sets the session and use direnv to load per-repo secrets.
Ravi: we usually recommend direnv + op read. Sample .envrc for the web repo: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(op read "op://Redwood/Dev/REDWOOD_API_KEY")` then `direnv allow`. direnv loads for both interactive shells and processes started by VSCode if VSCode is launched from the WSL session.
Jules: hmm, I don't love storing the token in a file. is direnv secure?
Priya: direnv executes locally and you should keep .envrc in .gitignore; the advantage is you can keep secrets in 1Password and only fetch them at shell start. we also have an internal helper script that checks TTL and refreshes the op session if needed.
OnboardingBot: Hi Jules - see internal doc: https://intranet/redwood/onboarding/wsl-setup for WSL tips, gpg transfer steps, and a sample .envrc.
Jules: thanks — one final thing: corporate CA blocks pulling images inside WSL, docker-compose errors with certificate verify failed. any known fixes?
Ravi: copy the corporate root CA into the distro CA store: `sudo cp /mnt/c/Users/you/ca.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp.crt && sudo update-ca-certificates`. then ensure Docker Desktop has the cert in its setting (Resources -> Proxy/Certificates) and WSL integration is enabled. restart docker.
Priya: also check that your distro is enabled under Docker Desktop -> Resources -> WSL Integration. some folks needed to toggle it off/on after updating certs.
Jules: this is super helpful. last: recommended VSCode extensions?
Ravi: Remote - WSL, ESLint, Prettier, GitLens, Docker, and our internal snippets extension. plus the 1Password extension if you prefer a GUI flow.
Jules: awesome, I'll try these steps and DM if I get stuck. thanks for the quick help! :heart:
Priya: welcome aboard and ping for a pairing sesh if needed.
Jules: much appreciated :thumbsup: "
